To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the quality of decisions is influenced by decision makers’ systematic information processing and (ii) decision makers’ trust in the analytics expert is a key factor for the adoption of the analytics expert’s advice.

(1) high levels of analytics expertise can have a negative impact on the systematic information processing mode, and (2) the systematic information processing behavior is positively related to decision quality.

(a) high levels of analytics support do not automatically lead to high quality decisions; (b) decision makers’ information-processing behavior plays a key role in decision quality; and (c) the trustworthiness of analytics experts plays an important role in decision quality.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of BI&A support on the decision process, the information processing modes of decision makers, and the decision quality of the decision outcome.
the effects of BI&A technology on decision quality and the underlying decision processes.
understanding the role of decision makers’ information search behavior, the influence of analytics experts, as well as the role of decision characteristics in BI&A-supported decisions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
BI&A support is not a silver bullet for improving decision quality. Rather, it depends on the characteristics of the decision situation and decision maker’s information
the effects of the BI&A technology are mediated by the decision maker’s mode of information processing behavior and the analytics expert’s trustworthiness.
the more analytic advice decision makers use, the higher is the quality of their decision outcomes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the quality of decision processes and outcomes depends on decision makers’ systematic information processing and the adoption of analytic information.
decision quality depends on the characteristics of decision processes and how decision makers utilize the information they receive.
the quality of decision processes is not only determined by BI&A technology, it also depends on the decision maker’s mode of information processing.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the effects of BI&A support on decision quality depend on the decision maker's information processing behavior, which in turn depends on the level of analytics elaboration and on the trustworthiness of analytics experts.

the quality of decision makers’ information processes and decision quality are not only determined by the quality of BI&A support but also depend on the characteristics of decision processes and how they influence decision makers’ processing of information.
the design of analytics support should not only consider the technology, but also the organization, characteristics and modes of decision processes.
